sources.title: Agent Console recovery-runtime
sources.locator: DaemonRequest handling 1540-1770, Unix cfg and process-local fallback; docs/compatibility.md platform table; src/web/control.rs prompt payload and PTY writes
sources.finding: macOS/Linux use a detached daemon; Windows uses process-local ConPTY. Daemon spawn deduplicates a live terminal id and leases gate writers, but prompt requests carry text without an idempotency key; this is not generic command replay protection. Browser and TUI can access the same PTY. No product-owned environment provisioning or run budget in config/model/runtime inventories.

sources.title: Agent Console recovery-summary
sources.locator: SummaryWorker, SUMMARY_TIMEOUT, run_with_timeout; config.rs SummaryConfig 110-150; app.rs summary queue/backoff 1960-2170
sources.finding: Same-provider summaries use a serial worker, a 90-second timeout, cancellation on shutdown, 30-second minimum interval and failure backoff, three failures before a 300-second provider circuit cooldown. Summary errors and process exit descriptions are retained for display. These controls apply to summary jobs, not arbitrary coding-agent task budgets.

sources.title: Agent Console recovery-storage
sources.locator: CachedSession/PersistedState and rotate_jsonl_if_full 467-483; src/prune.rs help and confirmation; src/model.rs Session; web/mod.rs routes 195-260
sources.finding: Session summaries, first prompts, aliases and archive flags persist locally in SQLite; JSONL event generations rotate at 256 KiB with one previous generation. Alerts are in memory; pane scrollback is 2000 rows and reconnect tail 128 KiB. Prune is explicit and macOS/Linux-only. Model, routes and UI have session records, but no task artifact gallery, code review gate, exact-revision shipping workflow, task audit export or spec store.

sources.title: Agent Console pinned telemetry source inspection
sources.locator: Cargo.toml lines 20-40 (runtime dependencies); bounded search of src/, website/, docs/ and README for telemetry, analytics, PostHog, Segment, Sentry, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Bugsnag, Datadog, gtag and crash reporting, and for HTTP clients (reqwest, ureq, hyper client, TcpStream::connect), excluding Cargo.lock, vendor/ and target/
sources.finding: The application declares no HTTP client dependency, and its source contains no analytics, crash-reporting or usage-upload code; axum only serves the local web client. The one telemetry-like hit is the website README saying no analytics is installed on the website.
